title: ci: Type Check runs 476 s median on every PR and merge group although its turbo cache is restored — measure the cache hit rate, fix the miss, and type-check affected packages only on PR and merge-queue runs (two-speed CI, objectstack#22998)
body:
Protects: this repository's required `Type Check` context, the published check-run name every PR and merge group of `@object-ui/*` passes through; this card keeps the name and cuts its wall.

Filed by the director seat (summon #37, `session_01LqNgdPZB2Jnr5HpGbaqLeB`) on the maintainer's word 「Type Check 的两张后续卡也立吧」 (2026-10-12), the follow-up objectui#12214 names. Filing gate ①: a measured defect with a named landing point. ⛔ Not a claim. Tier H: `.github/workflows/**`; the PR stays a draft until a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` member approves it.

## What is measured (29 completed `CI` runs, 16 `pull_request` + 8 `merge_group` + push, the jobs API, 2026-10-12)

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| `Type Check` job wall min / median / p90 / max | 2 / 10.3 / 12.4 / 13.4 min |
| step `Run type-check` (`pnpm type-check`) | 476 s median, 620 p90, 680 max (82 % of the job) |
| step `Restore Turbo Cache` | 2 s median (a two-second restore is a small or empty cache) |
| the other 30 steps (guards, `Type-check scripts/`, setup) | about 90 s together |

The cache keys look right on paper: `key: turbo-${{ runner.os }}-type-check-${{ github.sha }}`, `restore-keys: turbo-${{ runner.os }}-type-check-` then `turbo-${{ runner.os }}-`, saved whenever the exact key missed. `turbo.json` declares `type-check` with `cache: true`, `dependsOn: ["^build", "//#type-check:e2e"]` and inputs that include `$TURBO_ROOT$/scripts/vite-*.ts`. Yet the step re-executes for about 8 minutes on every run, so something defeats the replay: a root task (`//#type-check:e2e`) or a root-level input whose hash changes on every commit, a cache directory that is not `.turbo/cache`, or `pnpm type-check` not going through turbo for every package. Which one is this card's first measurement, not its premise.

## What to build (one PR, Tier H, draft until approved; lands after objectui#12214's PR, which edits the same file)

1. **Measure the miss:** one PR run with `turbo run type-check --summarize` (or the run summary) read for cache hit / miss per package and the hash inputs of a missed package; name the input or task that invalidates the hash in the PR body.
2. **Fix it** so unchanged packages replay from the restored cache (narrow the invalidating input, split the root task out of `dependsOn`, or point the cache at the directory turbo writes).
3. **Type-check affected-only on `pull_request` / `merge_group`:** the packages the diff affects and their dependents (`--affected` against the merge base, or `--filter=...[<base>]`), the whole workspace on `push` and the hourly `schedule` (the doctrine's full battery). Root-level changes (lockfile, `tsconfig*.json`, `turbo.json`, `package.json`) mean everything affected; state the rule in the workflow.
4. The job keeps its name `Type Check`; `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` and `scripts/check-required-check-set.mjs` stay green.

Expected: `Run type-check` from 476 s to about 60–120 s on a typical PR; after objectui#12214, `Type Check` is the PR's critical path (10.2 min), so the PR wall follows this card down to the Lint job (6 min).

## Acceptance
- `Type Check` median under 4 minutes on three consecutive merge groups and three PRs, read from the jobs API and written in the PR body with the before figures above.
- The turbo summary of one PR run shows cache hits for packages the diff did not touch.

Related: objectstack#22998 · objectui#12214 · objectui#12208 · `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`type-check` job) · `turbo.json`.
